groups.title: First-party extensions (coming soon)
groups.blurb: Official Caduceus extensions in development — same drag-in format as community extensions, maintained in-repo. They ship separately from built-ins so API keys, extra tools you install, and permissions stay explicit when you turn them on.

items.name: Google Translate
items.detail: Calls the Cloud Translation API with your key (billed per character). Coming as a first-party extension rather than a built-in that depends on an undocumented free endpoint.

items.name: Jira and Linear
items.detail: Issue search and quick actions over each product's API. Coming soon — you'll bring your own account; both products assume a paid team plan for real use.

items.name: Internet speed test
items.detail: Measure download/upload against an endpoint you choose. Coming as an extension so Caduceus does not silently consume someone else's bandwidth on your behalf.

items.name: Authy import
items.detail: Authy has no public API and desktop apps were discontinued in 2024. A first-party path is being explored with the same bar as any extension that touches 2FA material.

items.name: Starting a macOS Focus session
items.detail: macOS does not expose Focus directly; the supported route is a Shortcuts action. Coming as an extension that runs the Shortcut you configure.

items.name: Bluetooth device switching
items.detail: Connect a named Bluetooth device from the palette. Coming with an optional helper — macOS still has no supported public API for this.

items.name: Keyboard backlight control
items.detail: Adjust keyboard brightness where hardware allows. Coming as an extension; may require a helper because Apple provides no stable public API.

items.name: Per-application volume
items.detail: Set volume per app via CoreAudio. Coming as an extension — likely a separate helper or driver, not a single built-in command.

items.name: Downloading video from a website
items.detail: Wraps yt-dlp you install yourself. Coming soon — Caduceus will not bundle yt-dlp; site terms stay between you and the host.

items.name: Text expansion that types for you
items.detail: System-wide expansion needs a keyboard event tap and a dedicated opt-in. Coming as its own first-party extension after a focused security review — palette snippets stay the built-in alternative.

commandGroups.title: Window management
commandGroups.blurb: Snap, resize and move the frontmost window of any application. Needs the Accessibility permission, which Caduceus asks for once and never prompts for again.

items.name: Window: left half
items.detail: Fills the left half of the display the window is currently on, stopping at the menu bar and the Dock rather than sliding under them.

items.name: Window: right half
items.detail: Fills the right half of the current display. Pairs exactly with the left half — no gap, no overlap.

items.name: Window: top half
items.detail: Fills the upper half of the current display.

items.name: Window: bottom half
items.detail: Fills the lower half of the current display.

items.name: Window: top-left quarter
items.detail: One of four quarters that tile the usable screen area exactly.

items.name: Window: top-right quarter
items.detail: One of four quarters that tile the usable screen area exactly.

items.name: Window: bottom-left quarter
items.detail: One of four quarters that tile the usable screen area exactly.

items.name: Window: bottom-right quarter
items.detail: One of four quarters that tile the usable screen area exactly.

items.name: Window: first third
items.detail: The left third of the display. Thirds are computed to add up exactly, so three windows leave no seam.

items.name: Window: middle third
items.detail: The middle third of the display.

items.name: Window: last third
items.detail: The right third of the display.

items.name: Window: first two-thirds
items.detail: The left two-thirds — the wide half of a two-thirds/one-third split.

items.name: Window: last two-thirds
items.detail: The right two-thirds.

items.name: Window: maximize
items.detail: Fills the whole usable area of the display. Not macOS full screen — the window keeps its title bar and stays in the current Space.

items.name: Window: almost maximize
items.detail: 92% of the display, centred — large without hiding what is behind it.

items.name: Window: reasonable size
items.detail: Two-thirds of the display, centred. The size to put a window back to after it has been dragged somewhere odd.

items.name: Window: center
items.detail: Centres the window without changing its size — a move, not a resize.

items.name: Window: make bigger
items.detail: Grows the window by 10% around its own centre, stopping at the edges of the display.

items.name: Window: make smaller
items.detail: Shrinks the window by 10% around its own centre, stopping before it becomes too small to use.

items.name: Window: move to next display
items.detail: Moves the window to the next display, keeping where it sat proportionally — so a window in the top-right corner arrives in the top-right corner, whatever size the other screen is.

items.name: Window: move to previous display
items.detail: The same, in the other direction.

items.name: Window: toggle full screen
items.detail: Enters or leaves macOS full screen — the green-button behaviour, with its own Space.

commandGroups.title: System
commandGroups.blurb: macOS settings, the Finder, power and the session — driven by the tools macOS already ships, so none of it needs anything installed.

items.name: Toggle dark mode
items.detail: Switches macOS between light and dark appearance. Needs permission to control System Events, which macOS asks for the first time.

items.name: Toggle Stage Manager
items.detail: Turns Stage Manager on or off and restarts the window manager so the change takes effect immediately.

items.name: Toggle hidden files in Finder
items.detail: Shows or hides dotfiles, then restarts Finder.

items.name: Toggle desktop icons
items.detail: Hides everything on the desktop, or brings it back. Nothing is moved or deleted — Finder just stops drawing it.

items.name: Restart Finder
items.detail: Relaunches Finder. The usual fix when a mounted volume will not go away.

items.name: Restart the Dock
items.detail: Relaunches the Dock, which also resets Mission Control and Stage Manager.

items.name: Restart the menu bar
items.detail: Relaunches SystemUIServer, which redraws the menu bar extras when one gets stuck.

items.name: Lock the screen
items.detail: Locks immediately, the same as the Apple menu's Lock Screen — regardless of the password delay set for sleep.

items.name: Turn the display off
items.detail: Puts the display to sleep without sleeping the machine, so anything running keeps running.

items.name: Sleep
items.detail: Puts the Mac to sleep.

items.name: Start the screen saver
items.detail: Starts the screen saver straight away.

items.name: Log out
items.detail: Ends the session. Applications are asked to save first, as they would be from the Apple menu.

items.name: Restart
items.detail: Restarts the Mac.

items.name: Shut down
items.detail: Shuts the Mac down.

items.name: Brightness up
items.detail: Raises display brightness by synthesising the hardware key, which is the only route Apple has not broken. Needs the Accessibility permission.

items.name: Brightness down
items.detail: Lowers display brightness. Needs the Accessibility permission.

commandGroups.title: Developer tools
commandGroups.blurb: Encoders, hashes, identifiers, formatters and inspectors. Every one of these runs locally, which is the point — a JWT or an API payload should never be pasted into a website to be read.

items.name: Generate a UUID
items.detail: A random version-4 UUID, copied as soon as it appears.

items.name: Generate ten UUIDs
items.detail: Ten version-4 UUIDs, one per line, for seeding fixtures.

items.name: Generate a ULID
items.detail: A ULID: a 48-bit millisecond timestamp followed by 80 random bits, in Crockford base32. Sorts by creation time, which is why you would use one instead of a UUID as a database key.

items.name: Generate a Nano ID
items.detail: A 21-character URL-safe identifier — shorter than a UUID and safe to put in a path.

items.name: Generate a password
items.detail: 24 characters from the system's cryptographic random source, guaranteed to contain every character class. Leaves out l, I, O, 0 and 1, because a password nobody can read off a screen gets written down somewhere worse.

items.name: Base64 encode  ·  base64 …
items.detail: Encodes what you type to standard base64, with padding.

items.name: Base64 decode  ·  unbase64 …
items.detail: Decodes base64 back to text. Tolerates missing padding, embedded newlines and either alphabet, because pasted tokens rarely arrive clean.

items.name: Base64 encode (URL-safe)
items.detail: The URL-safe alphabet with no padding — what JWTs and data URLs use.

items.name: Base64 decode (URL-safe)
items.detail: Decodes the URL-safe alphabet back to text.

items.name: Hex encode  ·  hex …
items.detail: Each byte of the input as two lowercase hex digits.

items.name: Hex decode  ·  unhex …
items.detail: Hex back to text. Accepts `0x` prefixes and colon- or dash-separated bytes.

items.name: URL encode  ·  urlencode …
items.detail: Percent-encodes everything outside the unreserved set, so the result is safe anywhere in a URL.

items.name: URL decode  ·  urldecode …
items.detail: Reverses percent-encoding, and reads `+` as a space the way a query string means it.

items.name: HTML escape  ·  htmlescape …
items.detail: Escapes the five characters that change the meaning of markup.

items.name: HTML unescape
items.detail: Turns entities back into characters, resolving `&` last so `&lt;` comes back as `<` rather than `<`.

items.name: Decode a JWT  ·  jwt …
items.detail: Shows a token's header and payload, formatted, and says whether it has expired. The signature is *not* verified — that needs the key, and a tool that showed a tick without one would be worse than none. Nothing is sent anywhere.

items.name: Format JSON  ·  json …
items.detail: Pretty-prints JSON with two-space indentation, and names the parse error if it is not valid.

items.name: Minify JSON
items.detail: Strips every byte of whitespace and reports how many that saved.

items.name: Escape as a JSON string
items.detail: Wraps the input in quotes and escapes it, ready to paste into a JSON document.

items.name: Current timestamp
items.detail: The Unix time now, in seconds and milliseconds, with the ISO 8601 form alongside.

items.name: Convert a timestamp  ·  epoch …
items.detail: Reads an epoch number or a date and shows the other. Ten digits are treated as seconds and thirteen as milliseconds, which stays unambiguous until the year 2286.

items.name: Convert a colour  ·  color …
items.detail: Reads a colour in any notation people paste and shows hex, RGB and HSL — plus the WCAG contrast against white and black, so you know which one the text can be.

items.name: Convert number bases  ·  base …
items.detail: Shows one number in decimal, hex, octal and binary at once. Reads `0x`, `0b` and `0o` prefixes.

items.name: Random number  ·  random …
items.detail: A number in a range you give — `5-10`, `5 10` or a bare `100` meaning 1 to 100.

items.name: SHA-256 hash  ·  sha256 …
items.detail: Hashes the input with SHA-256 and copies the digest.

items.name: SHA-512 hash  ·  sha512 …
items.detail: Hashes the input with SHA-512.

items.name: SHA-1 hash  ·  sha1 …
items.detail: Hashes the input with SHA-1. Broken for signatures; still what git object ids use.

items.name: MD5 hash  ·  md5 …
items.detail: Hashes the input with MD5. Fine for checking a download, never for a password.

commandGroups.title: Text
commandGroups.blurb: Reshape whatever you type or paste: case, line order, counts and cleanup.

items.name: Lorem ipsum
items.detail: Three sentences of placeholder text.

items.name: Slugify  ·  slug …
items.detail: Lowercases and dashes the input into something safe for a URL, keeping accented letters intact.

items.name: Count words and characters  ·  count …
items.detail: Words, characters, lines, paragraphs, sentences and an estimated reading time.

items.name: Sort lines A→Z  ·  sort …
items.detail: Sorts the lines you paste, ignoring case.

items.name: Sort lines Z→A
items.detail: The same, reversed.

items.name: Remove duplicate lines  ·  dedupe …
items.detail: Keeps the first occurrence of each line and says how many went.

items.name: Reverse line order
items.detail: Last line first.

items.name: Shuffle lines
items.detail: Randomises line order with a Fisher-Yates shuffle over the system random source.

items.name: Number lines
items.detail: Prefixes each line with `1.`, `2.` and so on.

items.name: Join lines
items.detail: Collapses lines into one comma-separated line, dropping blanks.

items.name: Trim whitespace
items.detail: Removes leading and trailing whitespace from every line.

items.name: Count repeated lines
items.detail: How often each line appears, most frequent first — a `sort | uniq -c` you do not have to remember.

items.name: Change case: UPPER CASE  ·  upper …
items.detail: Everything uppercased. Handles camelCase humps, so an identifier converts the way you meant.

items.name: Change case: lower case  ·  lower …
items.detail: Everything lowercased. Handles camelCase humps, so an identifier converts the way you meant.

items.name: Change case: Title Case  ·  title …
items.detail: Each word capitalised, punctuation and spacing untouched. Handles camelCase humps, so an identifier converts the way you meant.

items.name: Change case: Sentence case  ·  sentence …
items.detail: Capitalises the first letter after every sentence terminator. Handles camelCase humps, so an identifier converts the way you meant.

items.name: Change case: snake_case  ·  snake …
items.detail: Words joined with underscores. Handles camelCase humps, so an identifier converts the way you meant.

items.name: Change case: kebab-case  ·  kebab …
items.detail: Words joined with dashes. Handles camelCase humps, so an identifier converts the way you meant.

items.name: Change case: camelCase  ·  camel …
items.detail: First word lowercase, the rest capitalised and joined. Handles camelCase humps, so an identifier converts the way you meant.

items.name: Change case: PascalCase  ·  pascal …
items.detail: Every word capitalised and joined. Handles camelCase humps, so an identifier converts the way you meant.

commandGroups.title: Files & Finder
commandGroups.blurb: Actions on the current Finder selection. Deletion always means the Trash, never an unrecoverable remove.

items.name: Empty the Trash
items.detail: Empties the Trash through Finder, so the usual warnings about locked items still apply.

items.name: Find a file
items.detail: Searches file names through Spotlight, so it answers from an index that already exists rather than walking the disk. Choosing a result reveals it in Finder.

items.name: Largest files
items.detail: The biggest files in your home folder, over 100 MB, newest measurement first. Also answered from the Spotlight index, so it returns immediately instead of spinning the disk. Choosing one reveals it in Finder.

items.name: Compress the Finder selection
items.detail: Zips what is selected in Finder into an archive beside it, using the same tool Finder's own Compress uses — so resource forks and extended attributes survive. Never overwrites an existing archive.

items.name: Expand the selected archive
items.detail: Unpacks the selected archives into folders beside them.

items.name: Move the Finder selection to the Trash
items.detail: Deletes through Finder, so it lands in the Trash and Cmd-Z puts it back.

items.name: Quick Look the Finder selection
items.detail: Opens the macOS preview panel for what is selected, without switching to Finder.

items.name: Open the Finder selection in Terminal
items.detail: Opens Terminal at the selected folder, or at the folder containing the selected file.

items.name: Copy the path of the Finder selection
items.detail: Copies the POSIX path of everything selected, one per line.

items.name: Open the latest download
items.detail: Opens the newest file in ~/Downloads, skipping the part-files browsers leave behind mid-download.

items.name: Copy the path of the latest download
items.detail: The same file, as a path on the clipboard.

items.name: Toggle Wi-Fi
items.detail: Turns Wi-Fi on or off on whichever interface is actually the Wi-Fi one — not a hardcoded en0.

items.name: Local IP addresses
items.detail: Every interface that has an address, labelled the way Network settings labels it, plus the default router.

items.name: Public IP address
items.detail: This machine's address as the internet sees it. The one command in Caduceus that deliberately leaves the machine — it runs only when you pick this row.

items.name: Wi-Fi details
items.detail: The network you are on, the address it gave you, the router and the interface name.

items.name: Look up a hostname  ·  dns …
items.detail: Resolves a hostname to its addresses using the system resolver.

items.name: Ping a host  ·  ping …
items.detail: Five packets, summarised as loss and round-trip time.

commandGroups.title: Developer environment
commandGroups.blurb: What is running on this machine: ports, repositories, SSH hosts and containers.

items.name: Listening ports
items.detail: Every process holding a TCP port open, with its pid. Choosing one stops it with SIGTERM, so a dev server flushes its logs and removes its socket rather than being killed outright. Type a number after the keyword to narrow to one port.

items.name: Git repositories
items.detail: Repositories under the usual project folders — Developer, Projects, Code, src, dev, repos and Documents/GitHub — with the branch each one is on. Choosing one opens it in Terminal. Only two levels deep, so it stays instant.

items.name: SSH hosts
items.detail: The hosts defined in ~/.ssh/config, with their hostname and user. Choosing one opens Terminal and connects. Wildcard patterns are skipped, because they are rules rather than machines you can reach.

items.name: Docker containers
items.detail: Every container, running or not, with its image and status. Choosing one starts or stops it. Says plainly whether Docker is missing or simply not running.

commandGroups.title: Utilities
commandGroups.blurb: The small things that are faster to type than to go and find.

items.name: Eject all disks
items.detail: Ejects every removable volume under /Volumes, and says which ones refused.

items.name: Keep this Mac awake  ·  awake …
items.detail: Opens the Keep Awake page: sessions that run indefinitely, for a duration, or until a time, with a live countdown — everything Amphetamine's core does, on the caffeinate macOS already ships. Or skip the page: `awake 45` and `awake 2h` start a timed session straight from here. Sessions are tied to Caduceus's process, so quitting the app always re-enables sleep.

items.name: Allow this Mac to sleep
items.detail: Ends the running keep-awake session immediately.

items.name: Define a word  ·  define …
items.detail: Looks a word up in the Dictionary app that ships with macOS. No network involved.

items.name: About this Mac
items.detail: Model, chip, cores, memory, macOS version, battery and uptime, on one screen and ready to paste into a bug report.

items.name: Check Caduceus's permissions
items.detail: Shows which of Accessibility and Screen Recording Caduceus currently holds, and whether the native helper is installed. Reads the state without prompting.

items.name: Clipboard history
items.detail: Everything you have copied — text, images, file paths — searchable and pinnable, kept in a local database that never leaves this Mac. The /v prefix filters it directly.

items.name: System monitor
items.detail: Live CPU, memory, disk and network, with the processes using them — and a way to end one that has stopped behaving.

items.name: Open the Manage window  ·  manage …
items.detail: The tabbed window for everything with live state: keep-awake sessions, sound devices, listening ports, Docker containers and this Mac's details. Tabs stay open while you use another, like a browser — ⌘1–⌘5 switch, ⌘W closes.
